themes.title: Guardant loses $245.2M TwinStrand judgment the same week its own Tempus suit survives dismissal
themes.description: A Delaware court entered final judgment for TwinStrand and the University of Washington against Guardant Health on Aug 21 (now on appeal, execution stayed), while a Co-CEO separately disclosed a multi-million-dollar stock sale. Days later, a judge refused to dismiss Guardant's own patent suit against Tempus AI, but pushed the Markman hearing from Aug 27 to Oct 20. The diagnostics layer's IP fights are now real money, not background noise.

themes.title: CRISPR Therapeutics' CTX310 sustains deep LDL and triglyceride cuts a year after one infusion
themes.description: Phase 1a data presented at ESC Congress 2026 and published simultaneously in NEJM showed a mean 79% reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 (max 89%), a mean 48% triglyceride cut and a mean 53% LDL cut at the highest dose, with no new safety signals. It's the most concrete durability evidence yet that in-vivo cardiovascular gene editing works beyond Casgevy's approved rare-disease indication — though it's still Phase 1a/1b, not an approval.

themes.title: Generate Biomedicines flips from below-offer to a 52-week high; Eikon stays the laggard
themes.description: Generate Biomedicines hit $19.81 (+12% in a session) on Aug 25 heading into its Aug 26 lock-up expiry, which it absorbed without cracking, now trading well above its $16 IPO price ahead of Sept 8 Phase 1b GB-0895 data. ARK made its largest ARKG buy of the week here (~$6.2M). Eikon Therapeutics had no comparable catalyst and remains well below its $18 offer — proof that 2026's AI-native IPO cohort is resolving name by name, not as a bloc.

themes.title: A single-day pullback (Aug 28) trimmed gains across every biotech benchmark at once
themes.description: ARKG fell 4.5%, XBI fell 3.5% and IBB fell 2.7% in one session, even as all three funds' trailing 1-year returns remain strongly positive (ARKG +92.7%, XBI +80.7%, IBB +51.2%). Separately, 20 biotech IPOs have now priced in 2026 (5 in August alone, 14 raising over $250M) and 2026 M&A has hit $106B across 201 deals — the fundamentals of the rally look intact, but the price action is a reminder of how fast concentrated gains can round-trip.

private_watchlist.name: Isomorphic Labs
private_watchlist.note: AlphaFold 3 lineage; Thrive Capital-led round adds MGX, Temasek, CapitalG & UK Sovereign AI Fund alongside Alphabet/GV. ISM8969 cleared FDA for human trials Jan 28, 2026 — the oncology candidate CEO Demis Hassabis says will anchor Isomorphic's first clinical trials by year-end 2026, a year later than his original 2025 target.

private_watchlist.name: Insilico Medicine
private_watchlist.note: Formally initiated the Phase III GENESIS-IPF trial for rentosertib on Jul 7, 2026 — 320 patients, 52 weeks, 47 centers across China; the Phase IIa data behind it (published in Nature Medicine) showed +98.4 mL forced vital capacity improvement at 12 weeks on the 60mg arm. Earned a second consecutive Prix Galien USA "Best Start-Up" nomination (Aug 18), recognizing rentosertib's Phase III advance and ~$10B in aggregate 2026 deal value. Still the field's clearest clinical proof point; listed on HKEX (Dec 2025, $292M IPO).

private_watchlist.name: Xaira Therapeutics
private_watchlist.note: Launched X-Cell, its first virtual cell model (4.9B parameters, trained on the X-Atlas/Pisces dataset), in March 2026. Built out its clinical leadership Jul 6 — Ci Chu to Chief Discovery Officer, Bo Wang to Chief AI Scientist — and added Rachel Lane as SVP, Business Development & Operations in August, continuing the shift from platform-building toward actually running trials.

private_watchlist.name: NewLimit
private_watchlist.note: Epigenetic reprogramming for longevity (Founders Fund, Lilly Ventures, Jun 2026); moved its first candidate medicine into large-scale manufacturing in January and has since run four large-scale screens turning up dozens of new payloads that restore youthful gene expression and regenerative function in old human liver cells, still targeting clinical entry as early as 2027. Retro Biosciences (Sam Altman-backed, $1.8B valuation, $3B+ raised) is reportedly raising a new ~$1B round to fund multiple longevity programs, on top of RTR242's ongoing Alzheimer's Phase 1 trial in Australia — CEO Joe Betts-LaCroix says it's going well with no dose-limiting toxicities so far.

bear_case.title: Biology still fails in the clinic
bear_case.description: Zero AI-discovered drugs have reached full FDA approval. Recursion's Q2 loss beat estimates but revenue is still shrinking; even CRISPR Therapeutics' genuinely durable CTX310 data (79% mean ANGPTL3 reduction at 1 year, published in NEJM) is gene editing, not an AI-discovery platform — the field's clearest recent clinical wins keep coming from outside the AI-native names on this page.

bear_case.title: IP litigation is now a balance-sheet risk, not a footnote
bear_case.description: Guardant Health was hit with a $245.2M final judgment in the TwinStrand/University of Washington patent case (Aug 21, under appeal), the same week its own offensive suit against Tempus survived a dismissal motion but had its Markman hearing pushed from Aug 27 to Oct 20. Patent risk cuts in both directions in the diagnostics layer, and it moves real money either way.

bear_case.title: Catalyst-driven volatility, in both directions
bear_case.description: Generate Biomedicines swung from trading below its $16 offer to a $19.81 52-week high in the same month, while Relay is +134.8% YTD despite a swollen dilution facility — proof these stocks can re-rate violently on sentiment alone. The Aug 28 session showed the same thing sector-wide: ARKG, XBI and IBB all dropped 2.7-4.5% in a single day even as trailing 1-year returns remain strongly positive.

bear_case.title: Hardware and instrument risk isn't just a biology problem
bear_case.description: Quantum-Si's Aug 13 disclosure that Proteus won't launch until Q2 2027 — a full year late — alongside a 20% workforce cut, is a reminder that the proteomics layer's timelines slip just like clinical ones. Compare that to Abbott's ~$21B all-cash purchase of Exact Sciences: real test volumes and reimbursed CPT codes command real M&A premiums, while unproven instrument platforms carry genuine execution risk regardless of the underlying science.

bear_case.title: Funding is recovering, but selectively
bear_case.description: 20 biotechs have IPO'd in 2026 (5 in August alone) versus 11 for all of 2025, with 14 raising over $250M — the strongest IPO cohort since 2021 — but about two-thirds of H1 2026 venture rounds still went to biotechs that already had a drug in human testing. Early-formation platforms remain comparatively starved of capital even as headline totals hit multi-year highs, and long-duration rate sensitivity can close the funding window unevenly.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Eli Lilly
positions.note: No new catalyst this week, but nothing has changed the thesis either: $85–87B FY26 guidance and five active AI partnerships (NVIDIA, Insilico, Chai Discovery and others) sit on top of a cash-generative base business that doesn't need any one platform to work.

positions.name: Novartis
positions.note: No new catalyst this week; Q2 sales +3% to $14.4B and reaffirmed guidance still stand, with the multi-partner AI strategy (Chai Discovery, Orionis, Relation Therapeutics) continuing to be funded by pharma economics rather than a platform story.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: BioNeMo and the Lilly co-innovation lab (~7 months into build-out, now with an expanded model set covering RNA structure, molecular synthesis and toxicity prediction) make it the compute layer for nearly every AI-biotech platform on this page. It also sits in your AI, Robotics and Quantum sleeves — don't double-count the exposure across sleeves.

positions.name: Illumina
positions.note: Entered ARKG's top 10 for the first time this week (4.08% weight, displacing Eli Lilly) even as ARK trimmed shares across its broader fund family on Aug 18 — the sequencing incumbent keeps monetizing every experiment regardless of which drug-discovery platform wins.

positions.name: Schrödinger
positions.note: Schrödinger is now seeking partners to advance SGR-1505 and SGR-3515 beyond Phase 1 rather than funding them independently — sensible capital discipline, but it also signals less confidence in running its own pivotal trials, so conviction comes down slightly even as ARK kept buying and shares stayed roughly flat YTD.

positions.name: Recursion
positions.note: Q2 loss of $0.25/share beat the $0.28 Street estimate, but Morgan Stanley trimmed its price target to $5.30 from $5.50 even as the broader Street average sits at $7.22 Overweight — cost discipline is improving faster than the revenue decline is being solved.

positions.name: Relay Therapeutics
positions.note: Shares are +134.8% YTD, vastly outperforming a roughly flat biotech industry — the market has clearly re-rated the Dynamo oncology platform well ahead of its early-2027 Phase 3 readout, even with the at-the-market facility expanded to ~$463M still a real dilution overhang.

positions.name: Generate Biomedicines
positions.note: Stock hit a 52-week high of $19.81 (+12% in a session) heading into its Aug 26 lock-up expiry, which it absorbed without cracking, ahead of Sept 8 Phase 1b GB-0895 data — ARK made its single largest ARKG purchase of the week here (~$6.2M) and GENB now trades meaningfully above its $16 IPO price.

positions.name: 908 Devices
positions.note: Raised the low end of FY26 guidance to $68–70M on a new NIRLAB acquisition plus 23% Q2 revenue growth — the most consistently strong tooling print on this page for a second straight quarter, still sized small because revenue remains single-digit millions.

positions.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
positions.note: CTX310's 1-year durability data — 79% mean ANGPTL3 reduction, 48% mean triglyceride cut, 53% mean LDL cut from one infusion, published in NEJM — is the clearest evidence yet that in-vivo cardiovascular editing works beyond Casgevy's rare-disease approval; upgraded from Watch to a small starter position given how early-stage (Phase 1a/1b) the readout still is.

positions.name: Tempus AI
positions.note: FDA cleared Tempus ECG-PH on Aug 24, extending its AI-diagnostic product line, but the Aug 27 ruling that let Guardant's patent suit against it proceed pushed the Markman hearing out to Oct 20 — a genuinely improving product story still living under an extended legal cloud, so still a Watch rather than a position.

positions.name: Guardant Health
positions.note: A Delaware court entered a $245.2M final judgment against Guardant in the TwinStrand/University of Washington patent case on Aug 21 (now on appeal), a Co-CEO disclosed a multi-million-dollar stock sale days later, and Guardant's own suit against Tempus drags on with its Markman hearing now pushed to Oct 20 — three simultaneous legal and governance overhangs on top of an already-rich valuation are enough to move this off Watch.

positions.name: Intellia Therapeutics
positions.note: No new company-specific catalyst this week; still waiting on the BLA filing for lonvo-z and analysts remain split (TipRanks Buy at $29 vs. Morgan Stanley Hold), so it stays a Watch rather than a position.

positions.name: Eikon Therapeutics
positions.note: No news this week to resolve the Aug 4 lock-up overhang or the board resignations that preceded the Aug 10 Merck-advisor addition; shares remain well below the $18 IPO price with no near-term catalyst.

positions.name: Quantum-Si
positions.note: No new information this week; the Aug 13 disclosure of a full-year Proteus delay to Q2 2027 and a 20% workforce cut still stands as the most material data point, so it remains an Avoid.
